svg.text: BLUEPRINT 07: GAUSS'S DIVERGENCE THEOREM, SURFACE CAPPING & VOLUMETRIC FLUX ENGINE
Closed Surface Outward Flux oiint F . dS • Volumetric Source Integral iiint (div F) dV • Open Capping • GATE 2023 Cone Deep Dive

g.text: Converts the total outward flux through closed boundary S into a 3D volume integral:
oiint_S F . dS = iiint_V ( div F ) dV = iiint_V ( grad . F ) dV
Must completely enclose a 3D solid volume V (Cube, Sphere, Cylinder, Cone).
Must point STRICTLY OUTWARD from enclosed volume V!
If flux asked is inward, multiply result by -1 !
If the divergence of F evaluates to a constant scalar c throughout volume V:
div(F) = c ==> oiint_S F . dS = iiint_V c dV = c x iiint_V dV
F = r = x i + y j + z k
Over sphere radius R: 3(4/3 pi R^3) = 4pi R^3
Zero net outward flux across ANY closed body.
Boundary: Curved lateral + 2 circular end caps
Boundary: Conical lateral + 1 base disk cap
Boundary: Curved dome + 1 flat circular base cap
Boundary: Parabolic bowl + 1 top circular cap
TETRAHEDRON BOUNDED BY COORDINATE PLANES & x/a + y/b + z/c = 1:
Directly eliminates triple integration over triangular pyramid limits!
HOW TO APPLY GAUSS'S THEOREM TO OPEN SURFACES
Problem: Gauss's Theorem strictly requires a CLOSED surface. What if GATE asks for flux through an OPEN surface S_open?
oiint_(S_total) F . dS = iint_(S_open) F . dS + iint_(S_cap) F . dS = iiint_V (div F) dV
==> iint_(S_open) F . dS = iiint_V (div F) dV - iint_(S_cap) F . dS
integral of div F over V.
Trivial if div F is constant!
iint_(dome) F . dS = iiint_V (div F) dV - iint_(disk) F . (-k) dx dy
If field F has F_z = 0 at z = 0 (e.g., F = x i + y j + 2z k => F_z(0)=0):
Flux through Dome == iiint_V (div F) dV EXACTLY!
Rule of Thumb: Whenever flat base sits at z=0 and F_z(0)=0, Flat Cap Flux vanishes!
Use Gauss's Divergence Theorem immediately! Evaluate div F.
If div F = 0 => Answer = 0! If div F = const => Answer = const x Volume!
2. IS THE SURFACE OPEN WITH A SIMPLE BOUNDARY?
Is F already written as a Curl (F = grad x A)? If YES => Use Stokes' Theorem!
iint_S F . dS = iint_S (grad x A) . dS = oint_C A . dl (Line integral over boundary loop C)!
3. IS F NOT A CURL, BUT ENCLOSES AN OPEN CAVITY?
Use Surface Capping! Add flat cap, apply Gauss's Theorem, subtract cap flux.
Direct surface integration on curved surfaces is always the SLOWEST route!
"A vector field B(x, y, z) = x i + y j - 2z k is defined over a conical region
having height h = 2, base radius r = 3, as shown. The base of the cone lies
in the x-y plane and is centered at the origin. If n denotes unit outward normal
to curved surface S of the cone, the value of iint_S B . n dS equals _______."
Step 1: Test the Divergence of Vector Field B:
The vector field B is STRICTLY SOLENOIDAL everywhere in R^3!
Step 2: Total Closed Surface Flux via Gauss's Theorem:
oiint_(S_total) B . dS = iiint_V (grad . B) dV = iiint_V (0) dV = 0
Step 3: Partition Closed Surface into Curved S + Flat Base S_1:
oiint_(S_total) B . dS = iint_(S_curved) B . dS + iint_(S_base) B . dS = 0
==> iint_(S_curved) B . dS = - iint_(S_base) B . dS
Step 4: Evaluate Base Disk Flux iint_(S_base) B . dS:
On the base: z = 0 and unit outward normal n_cap = -k
B . n_cap = (x i + y j - 2z k) . (-k) = +2z
GATE EXAM PSYCHOLOGICAL TRAP IN THIS PROBLEM:
1. Students waste 15 minutes setting up the cone surface equation:
z = 2 - (2/3) sqrt(x^2 + y^2) and computing dS = sqrt(1 + z_x^2 + z_y^2) dx dy
2. They attempt nasty polar conversions with r dr dtheta on an inclined frustum!
Always check div F FIRST! div B = 0 => Total Flux = 0.
Check base z=0 => B . (-k) = 2(0) = 0 => Base flux = 0 => Curved flux = 0!
Solved in 20 seconds with absolute 100% mathematical certainty!
